title: Kenyan Chicken Pepper Fry
community: Popular across Kenya — especially among spice lovers
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Chicken Pepper Fry — chicken pieces boldly seasoned with crushed black pepper, fresh chilli, garlic, ginger, and spices then pan-fried until deeply caramelised and intensely flavourful. For those who like their chicken with real heat and character.
longDesc: Kuku wa pilipili is chicken for pepper lovers — where most Kenyan chicken dishes lean mild to medium, pepper fry leans into heat and boldness. Crushed black pepper and fresh chilli dominate the seasoning, supported by garlic, ginger, and a concentrated tomato base that caramelises around each piece during the high-heat finishing stage.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces — cut into small pieces
2 fresh green or red chillies — finely chopped
steps: Season chicken with salt, paprika, cumin, and half the crushed pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over high heat. Sear chicken pieces for 4—5 minutes per side until deeply browned. Remove.
In the same pan, cook onions until golden — 6 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and chillies. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook for 5—6 minutes until thick.
Add remaining crushed pepper. Stir 30 seconds.
Return chicken. Toss to coat. Cook for 10—12 minutes until chicken is cooked through and the sauce has caramelised around each piece.
Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Crush the peppercorns coarsely rather than grinding finely — the larger pieces give pockets of intense heat.
The sauce should caramelise and cling rather than stay saucy.
Reduce heat if needed during the final stage to prevent burning.
commonMistakes: Using pre-ground pepper only — loses the bold, coarse character that defines pepper fry.
Not cooking out the tomatoes fully — the sauce stays acidic and raw-tasting.

faqs.a: Pepper fry is moderately to strongly hot, depending on the amount of chilli used. Reduce the chilli for a milder version — the crushed black pepper gives warmth without sharp heat.

cookingScience: Black pepper contains piperine, which activates the same heat receptors as capsaicin (from chilli). Crushing rather than grinding peppercorns releases the essential oils more slowly during cooking, producing a different — more rounded — heat profile than fine-ground pepper.
sustainabilityTips: This dish works well with chicken offcuts and less popular pieces like wings and necks.
reheating: Reheat quickly in a hot pan.
healthBenefits: Black pepper contains piperine which enhances absorption of curcumin from other spices.
Chilli provides capsaicin with anti-inflammatory properties.
culturalNote: Chicken pepper fry reflects the spice-loving side of Kenyan cuisine — a dish for those who appreciate bold heat and concentrated flavour in their everyday cooking.
regionalVariations: Mild version — reduced pepper and no chilli.
Dry pepper fry — sauce fully reduced.
